'''Jan  Švec''' (born 22 November 1966) is a Czech voice scientist.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cesta k umělým hlasivkám. [Journey towards artificial vocal folds] |url=http://www.ceskatelevize.cz/program/port/600-cesta-k-umelym-hlasivkam/video/ |work=[[Czech Television]] |date=October 10, 2010 |access-date=October 26, 2010 | first=Tereza | last=Pultarová}}</ref> He is the [[Invention|inventor]] of [[videokymography]], a method for [[High speed photography|high-speed]] [[Scientific visualization|visualization]] of [[Vocal folds|vocal-fold]] [[Phonation|vibrations]], which is being used for advanced [[Medical diagnosis|diagnosis]] of [[List of voice disorders|voice disorders]].

As of 2011, Jan G. Švec has written over 140 [[Scientific literature|publications]] (over 40 as first author) in various areas of voice research:<ref>Jan Švec's profile on ResearcherID – http://www.researcherid.com/rid/C-6909-2008</ref><ref>Full list of publications by Jan Švec – http://sites.google.com/site/jangsvec/publications</ref> visualization of vocal fold vibration through videokymography; voice [[Vocal register|registers]]; singing voice; [[methodology]] of voice [[measurement]]; voice dosimetry; determination of [[Biomechanics|biomechanical]] properties of vocal folds; vocal fold and [[vocal tract]] [[Mathematical model|modelling]]; [[Clinical research|clinical]] measurement of voice; and [[Scientometrics|scientometry]].

Jan G. Švec was born 22.11.1966 in [[Olomouc]], Czech Republic. He received his MSc (1990: [[Palacký University of Olomouc|Palacký University]], Olomouc) in fine mechanics and [[optics]], and two PhD degrees in biophysics (1996: Palacký University, Olomouc) and [[medical science]]s (2000: [[University of Groningen]]). From 1995 to 1999, he worked as assistant professor at the Institute for Postgraduate Medical Education, Prague, Czech Republic. In 2001–2004 he was a Visiting Research Professor at the [[National Center for Voice and Speech]], Denver Center for the Performing Arts, Denver, CO, USA and in 2004–2007 a research scientist at the Groningen Voice Research Lab, Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of Groningen, the [[Netherlands]]. Since 2007, he has been a scientist and lecturer at the Department of Biophysics, Palacký University, Olomouc, Czech Republic and also a research scientist at the Voice Centre Prague.

In 2004–2010 he was the chair of the Voice Committee of the International Association of Logopedics and Phoniatrics (IALP). He serves as the deputy editor-in-chief for [[Vocology|Logopedics Phoniatrics Vocology]], Taylor & Francis, and is a member of the editorial board of the Journal of Voice, Elsevier Medical Journals. He is a Distinguished Alumnus of the Palacký University in Olomouc, the Czech Republic.
